body:
Review baseline: `625ecfd5e9ff...0bb885f2519d`

**[P1] Retry persistence after budget space is freed**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/headless.rs:954` returns `Ok(())` forever after one
`BudgetExhausted`. Another process can clear old sessions, as the recovery hint suggests, but this
process never probes again. Every later turn is then reported successful while its transcript is
silently not persisted. Please separate one-time notice suppression from retry eligibility, and
add a regression that exhausts the budget, frees space, then persists a later turn through
`SessionRuntime`.

**[P1] Serialize the per-user capacity check with the write**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store.rs:175` decides that the incoming session fits
before `write_atomic`, without a session-root lock spanning the scan and write. With 90 MiB stored,
two processes can each admit a new 8 MiB session from the same snapshot and finish at 106 MiB, so
the 100 MiB cap is not enforced. Please add a per-user lock or reservation held through the write,
plus a synchronized two-writer regression.

**[P1] Protect a running session during its first turn after a long idle**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store.rs:223` deletes any unlocked envelope at the age
cutoff. A long-lived core holds no session lock between turns, so after seven days another process
can sweep its envelope while the next user turn is running. That turn then commits against a
missing generation and returns `Conflict`, losing the work; the resume-time stamp does not cover an
already-running process. Please add a process-lifetime activity lease or a start-of-turn stamp, and
regress this with a long-lived runtime plus a concurrent sweep.

Review baseline: `82eac898c042...e5a6e0d98652`

**[P1] Restore the session-recovery integration suite**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store.rs:163` creates `.budget.lock` directly under the
session root. Existing integration helpers treat every root entry as a scope directory, so
`cargo test -p cosh-core --test session_recovery` now fails 3 of 22 cases with
`Not a directory`; the PR's `Test cosh-ng` job reproduces the same failures. Please update every
scope-discovery helper to filter for scope directories (including the two-scope case), and keep
this integration target in the validation set.

**[P1] Claim the live lease before touching a resumed session**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/headless.rs:906-943` loads and re-commits a resumed envelope
before taking its lease, while `session/scoped.rs:241` waits on that process-lifetime lock. If
process A is already using the session, process B first advances the stored generation and then
blocks until A exits; A's next commit sees B's generation and loses the turn with `Conflict`.
Please claim the lease non-blockingly before load/re-stamp, and regress that a second resume
returns promptly without changing the envelope while the first runtime can still commit.

**[P1] Make the activity-lease handoff atomic**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/headless.rs:997-999` releases the session and budget locks before
the first lease is acquired. Also, `session/scoped.rs:271` drops a successful eviction-side lease
probe before `store.rs:1263-1278` locks and deletes the envelope. Under capacity pressure, another
writer can therefore delete a just-successfully committed session before its runtime leases it;
the first writer reports success while its envelope is gone. A resume can likewise acquire its
lease after the probe but still be deleted. Please hold the runtime lease across the first write
handoff and retain the eviction-side lease guard through deletion, with synchronized regressions.

**[P2] Label the refusal size as projected, not stored**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store.rs:240` assigns `projected` to `total_bytes`, but
`session.rs:233-234` and its display text call that value currently accounted bytes. It includes
the unwritten incoming envelope and excludes the old envelope being replaced, so the user can be
told that more bytes are stored than actually exist. Please name or render it as the projected
post-commit total and pin that wording in the refusal regression.

Review baseline: `46728ecd5d16...b76c4aaa6512`

**[P1] Anchor the budget to the user, not the selected persistence root**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store.rs:94` derives the lock and accounting root from
the configurable `persist_dir`, while the scan at line 336 only visits 24-hex children of that one
root. Two workspaces that set `persist_dir = "project-sessions"` therefore receive independent
100 MiB caps. Supported legacy JSON under `workspace/sessions`, or flat in a relative root, is also
never counted or aged. This makes the fixed per-user 7-day/100 MiB bound bypassable and leaves
upgrades unbounded. Possible direction: use one user-global budget namespace and include or migrate
legacy entries; regress two workspace-relative roots plus pre-existing legacy bytes.

**[P1] Remove leases created for failed resumes**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/headless.rs:907` creates `.<id>.live` before `load` proves
that the envelope exists. Resuming any valid but missing UUID returns `not_found` but leaves it;
`SessionLock::drop` only unlocks it, and budget cleanup ignores control files. Repeated misses can
therefore consume unbounded inodes and make every globally locked budget scan slower. Please unlink
the just-created lease on load failure while its guard is held, and regress that a missing resume
leaves no new control file.

**[P1] Coordinate explicit clears with the budget snapshot**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store.rs:379` turns a vanished candidate into `Io`, while
`clear` removes it at line 926 without the per-user budget lock. If process B clears another session
during process A's scan, an unlink between `read_dir` and `symlink_metadata` makes A's completed
turn fail persistence; an unlink just after metadata leaves stale bytes and can report
`BudgetExhausted` even though space was freed. Please coordinate clear with the snapshot or retry
disappearing candidates, with a synchronized clear-versus-commit regression.

Review baseline: `b48488cad57b...64bec0072197`

**[P1] Isolate unit-test budgets from the real HOME namespace**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/headless.rs:1639` builds test stores with the
production budget namespace. Every `persist` therefore updates the invoking user's
fixed HOME index and scans its default and registered roots, so a normal local test
run can age out real sessions. The parallel tests also delete each other's fixtures:
`cargo test -p cosh-core --bin cosh-core headless::tests` failed 13/14 here because
the long-lived-runtime sweep removed the backdated resume fixture before it could be
leased; the exact test and the full target with `--test-threads=1` both passed.
Please inject a unique temporary budget namespace into every in-process test store,
including the common store helper, and keep the default parallel target as regression
coverage.

Review baseline: `e600b199b7ca...6b89f8b62591`

**[P1] Remove controls after a rejected first commit**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/headless.rs:992` retains the newly created live lease before
the first persist attempt. If that attempt returns `BudgetExhausted`, the process exits without
an envelope. Dropping the lease only releases its `flock`; it never unlinks `.<id>.live`.
`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store.rs:481` also creates `.<id>.lock` before
budget admission, with no cleanup on this error path. Repeated fresh sessions while live history
fills the cap therefore leave two control inodes per attempt. Every later budget scan walks those
entries, and eventually the session store can run out of inodes. The failed-resume cleanup does
not cover this path.

Possible direction: track controls created before the first successful envelope and remove them
under the budget lock with the existing inode guard when an uncommitted runtime exits. Please
regress a budget-refused fresh process, wait for its exit, and assert that neither control remains.

Review baseline: `966ce08b7d1c...e599d2aaddd5`

**[P1] Clean controls after every failed first commit**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/headless.rs:999` only releases the fresh live lease for
`BudgetExhausted`, and `src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store.rs:596` applies the same
restriction to the generation lock. If a registered scope is unreadable, the existing
`activity::unreadable_scope_refuses_new_optional_persistence` path returns `Io` after both
control files were created. The fresh process exits without an envelope but leaves
`.<id>.live` and `.<id>.lock`; repeating the command consumes two inodes per session and makes
every later budget walk scan the debris. Possible direction: guard all newly created controls
until the first envelope lands, cleaning them on every pre-commit error while preserving
pre-existing or replaced inodes. Extend the unreadable-scope process test to assert both
controls are absent after exit.

Review baseline: `69ae39dc5b97...41df304df107`

**[P1] Restrict legacy cleanup to directories owned by this store**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store/budget.rs:35` registers
`<workspace>/sessions` for every configuration, but `SessionStore::for_workspace` only treats
that directory as legacy when the default persistence root is selected. With an absolute custom
`persist_dir`, a later budget sweep can therefore treat an unrelated
`sessions/<uuid>.json` message array as Cosh history and unlink it once it is seven days old or
capacity needs it, even though load, list, and clear would never claim it. Possible direction:
derive budget legacy locations from the same ownership predicate as `legacy_dirs` (or require a
durable ownership marker), and regress an absolute custom root with an old UUID message array
under `workspace/sessions` that must survive the sweep.

Review baseline: `69ae39dc5b97...a30380d15ade`

**[P1] Revalidate historical paths before granting deletion authority**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store/budget.rs:116` only appends or merges
pathnames, and `scopes` later trusts every saved path forever. After a user runs with the
default or a relative store, removes that directory, and another tool recreates the same path
with UUID-named JSON, a later Cosh commit can classify those unrelated files as legacy and
unlink them by age or capacity. This also happens after switching to an absolute store, whose
load/list/clear paths no longer own that directory. Canonicalization proves location, not
ownership continuity.

Possible direction: require a durable Cosh ownership marker or directory generation before
honoring a historical entry. Regress register, remove/recreate, then switch roots and assert
the unrelated file's bytes, inode, mode, and mtime remain unchanged.

**[P1] Validate modern envelopes before deleting them**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store.rs:1374` accepts any JSON object with a numeric
`updated_at_ms`; `envelope_commit_clock` does not validate the schema, filename ID, or required
session fields. A future `schema_version: 2` envelope, or a corrupt current envelope with an old
clock, is therefore deleted by the next age/capacity sweep even though normal loading rejects it
as incompatible or corrupt. This lets an older binary destroy session data it cannot interpret.

Possible direction: validate the current schema, matching session ID, and complete envelope
before using its clock. Add future-schema and malformed-current regressions that assert the
original bytes remain unchanged after a sweep.

Review baseline: `69ae39dc5b97...8e13db4be2df`

**[P1] Keep previously owned legacy bytes in the budget**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store/budget.rs:311` skips the whole legacy scope
when a recorded owner marker is missing, changed, or has unsafe permissions. Starting with a
default or relative legacy directory near 100 MiB, remove or chmod its marker and commit again.
The same directory's arrays disappear from `accounted`, so new envelopes can take the user over
the fixed cap while those bytes remain on disk. Lost deletion proof should make the entries
non-evictable, not unaccounted. Possible direction: retain entries when device/inode still match
but expose no eviction generation, and add a cap-pressure regression for marker loss.

**[P1] Lease the source session for the full compaction attempt**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/compaction/engine.rs:248` loads the session and then runs the
provider without taking the new activity lease. If a manually selected session is older than the
retention cutoff and the provider is still running, a commit in another process can sweep its
envelope; the final reload at line 341 then returns `not_found` after the active compaction has
already spent the provider call. Hold the live lease from before the initial load through the
final persist, and regress a blocked compactor racing a sweep through the production path.

**[P1] Do not open historical workspaces that own no legacy data**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store/budget.rs:261` opens every recorded workspace
before examining `location.legacy`. A normal workspace with no `sessions` directory is stored
with `legacy=[]`; if that old workspace later becomes unreadable or is replaced by a symlink,
every commit in every other workspace fails with `io`, even though all modern roots remain fully
measurable. Skip the workspace lookup for empty legacy sets, or separate modern roots from legacy
ownership records, and add a two-workspace regression with an inaccessible stale workspace.

**[P2] Roll back workspace artifacts after a missing resume**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store.rs:217` registers the workspace and creates its
hashed scope before `load` proves that the requested session exists. The failure cleanup at line
226 only removes the `.live` file. Missing resumes from distinct temporary workspaces therefore
leave one empty directory and one permanent location-index row each; the index is capped at
32 MiB, so enough misses eventually reject persistence for every new workspace. Check existence
under the global lock before registration/creation, or remove newly created empty state, and add
a distinct-workspace regression that keeps both the index and root cardinality stable.

Review baseline: `69ae39dc5b97...60d3498bb37f`

**[P1] Avoid rescanning the whole scope for every budget candidate**

`src/cosh-ng/crates/cosh-core/src/session/store.rs:1420-1421` constructs a fresh
`ScopedStorage` and calls `directory(true)` inside the per-entry loop. Each fresh
storage has `swept=false`, so `session/scoped.rs:81-90` runs
`sweep_stale_temporary_files`, which enumerates the entire scope. With n small sessions,
one age or capacity pass therefore performs n full directory walks while holding the
global budget lock. A valid 100 MiB store with many small envelopes can make first
commits and hourly rescans appear hung, while every other session waits for that lock.
Possible direction: cache each activity storage/directory for the whole pass, or add a
no-sweep directory path for lock probing. Please add an instrumented regression proving
that one pass sweeps each activity directory once, not once per candidate.

Review baseline: `69ae39dc5b97...4cf6aeb8ed47`

Remaining risks:

- Real-provider, installed RPM, dual-architecture, and manual terminal paths were not exercised.

Verification scope:

- Reviewed the full base/head diff and adjacent session, budget, compaction, and recovery code.
- Read all paginated conversation comments, reviews, inline replies, and timeline events.
- GraphQL reported zero review threads; the triggering review-request event was present.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed.
- Targeted budget, activity, quota, and compaction checks passed: 41 tests total.
